brief: Midterm elections produced a blue sweep, but the market reversed after Trump signaled willingness to work with Democrats. The author draws two conclusions: anti-AI regulation will likely slow capex, and the Iran war's unpopularity has eroded the oil risk premium toward a priced-in accelerated end to the conflict. European tech flows turned bearish on AI spending concerns and multiples compressed; the author argues the risk is an inventory glut across chips, turbines, cooling and electrical equipment rather than demand destruction, since existing energized compute becomes more valuable (less capex, higher FCF for hyperscalers) as expansion is constrained. Separately, physical Brent collapsed to a record discount to Dated Brent and into contango, pricing an end to the war, which the author flags as possibly running ahead of confirmed resolution. Gold is read as an inverse-oil trade: central banks drew down reserves to fund energy costs and resume buying as oil falls, making long gold a more defensible de-escalation trade than shorting oil. VIX and VXN both fell sharply; the author calls this rotation, not liquidation, with nets low enough that the broader market should not fall easily.
